name: How do construction loans work for multifamily development in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What do lenders usually require for a new apartment construction loan in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What do lenders usually require for a new apartment construction loan in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A construction loan for multifamily development is usually drawn in stages as the project progresses. Lenders generally want to see a complete budget, a credible source of equity, a strong borrower team, permits or a clear path to them, and a realistic exit strategy through sale or refinance. Interest reserves are often built into the financing so the project can carry debt during construction and early lease-up. In Los Angeles, lenders may be especially cautious about entitlement uncertainty, cost overruns, and parking-driven design complexity. That means the borrower often needs more documentation than on a simpler stabilized acquisition. A clean borrower package should include plans, a permit status summary, hard and soft cost breakdowns, contingency, timelines, and comparable rents. Developers should compare lender requirements early because one financing structure may work for a well-entitled site while another is better for a riskier infill parcel.
acceptedAnswer.description: Construction lenders typically want a detailed budget, experienced sponsor, equity contribution, contingency reserve, interest reserve, and a believable exit plan. Loan proceeds usually fund the project in draws as work is completed, not all at once. The lender may also require updated appraisals, permits, and a guaranteed completion structure.
